tinystream now has a desktop app. It's Linux-only for now, and it plays nearly everything as-is through mpv, so your server barely has to transcode, and subtitles keep up with the picture far better than they can in a browser. This release also adds NVENC transcoding and Android music, plus a long list of playback and library fixes for the server and the web app.

## Desktop app

The desktop app ([#144](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/pull/144)) is built in Rust with [iced](https://github.com/iced-rs/iced). It embeds libmpv and draws subtitles with [rustyass](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/rustyass), so you get the same styled ASS subtitles as on the web, kept in step with each frame. It's meant to look and feel like the web app, and has:

- Shows, movies, music and books, with the home page, libraries, title pages, Wanted, the calendar, Downloads, requests, settings and administration rebuilt after the web app.
- Hardware decoding with VA-API on AMD and Intel and NVDEC on NVIDIA, falling back to the CPU.
- Picture-in-picture, media keys (MPRIS), a tray icon, and screens that stay awake while you watch.
- Watch Together and Listen Together, with `tinystream://` invite links that open straight in the app.
- Clips: the clips page, the clip player and the full editor.
- Music: the library, albums, artists and playlists, the pill player, Now Playing tinted from the cover, lyrics, queue editing, gapless playback, crossfade and ReplayGain.
- A book reader with chapters, text sizes, focus mode and quotes.
- Passkey sign-in with your security key, and passkey management in settings.
- Offline downloads: keep titles, seasons, episodes, albums and playlists on your computer, and watch or listen to them while your server can't be reached.

Download `tinystream-desktop-0.40.0-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` and run `./install.sh` from it to add the app to your menu (`--prefix /usr/local` installs it for everyone), or grab the AppImage and run it as-is. You'll need x86_64 Linux with glibc 2.39 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 40, or any rolling distribution), Wayland or X11, and a Vulkan driver.

## Server

- **NVENC transcoding** ([#98](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/issues/98)). Set `hardware = "nvenc"` under `[transcode]`, or leave it on `auto`, and `cuda-device` if you have more than one GPU. Live streams and clips scale on the GPU, and if hardware decoding fails on a file, tinystream decodes on the CPU and still encodes with NVENC. Docker users can add `docker-compose.nvidia.yaml`, which needs the NVIDIA Container Toolkit:

  ```sh
  docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml -f docker-compose.nvidia.yaml up -d
  ```

- **Offline downloads are now a permission.** Keeping copies of files on a device, whether a video, a song or its FLAC version, needs the new **Offline downloads** permission, which is off by default. Admins always have it; give it to others under People. Streaming isn't affected.
- Progress and plays now carry when they happened, so offline progress synced later doesn't overwrite something newer.
- A Range file endpoint for clients that play the original file directly.
- Changing a Watch Together room's episode now starts the next one playing, even if the last one was paused.
- Live transcodes of HDR video are tone mapped to SDR ([#71](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/issues/71)).
- VP9 reports its real profile and bit depth instead of always 8-bit Profile 0 ([#72](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/issues/72)).
- Adding, renaming or removing an external subtitle shows up without rescanning the video ([#74](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/issues/74)), and external subtitles only match their own video, so `Episode1.ass` no longer turns up on `Episode10` ([#76](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/issues/76)).
- Managed renames and undo keep everyone's resume positions and watched states ([#65](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/issues/65)).
- A library scan that can't read some folders no longer deletes what's in them from the catalog ([#63](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/issues/63)).
- Partly failed imports show their errors and can be retried without redoing what already worked ([#64](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/issues/64)).

## Web app

- A rebuilt title page, built around its episodes, with a sliding switcher for seasons and library filters.
- A tidier Wanted page, with each show's poster and backdrop, tidier downloads and a quieter calendar.
- The home banner fits its text.
- Playback that stalls retries on its own instead of buffering forever ([#66](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/issues/66)), a stream that ends early no longer skips to the next episode ([#68](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/issues/68)), and stream errors show up in the player ([#70](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/issues/70)).
- The player's controls hide again after moving to the next episode ([#101](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/issues/101)).
- Music recovers when its audio engine fails to start instead of getting stuck ([#77](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/issues/77)), and the queue keeps going past four tracks and on repeat one.
- Title pages, library events and reconnects no longer leave stale data on screen ([#73](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/issues/73)), Downloads updates right away ([#75](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/issues/75)), and a cleared Manual Match search stays cleared ([#67](https://github.com/tinystream-dev/tinystream/issues/67)).
- The volume down key unmutes like volume up, `S` skips the opening only without Shift, and a seek only flashes when the room allowed it.
- The book reader's selection menu shows up once you've finished selecting, under where the selection ends.

## Android

- Music: browsing, the mini player, Now Playing, lyrics, queue editing and playback settings, with a media notification and lock-screen controls.
- Admins can allow offline downloads for people.
